title: Broken Stele of the Sand Sea
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: Under the sunset, archaeologist Aida（A woman archaeologist in her early thirties, wearing a wide-brim canvas hat and goggles, khaki explorer kit, a magnifying glass around her neck, hands often dusted with sand） brushes yellow sand from the reliefs on the ruin stone gate（An ancient ruin stone gate half-buried in a dune, reliefs on the lintel, broken columns on both sides, sunset stretching long shadows）.

A row of five red survey flags（A row of five small red survey flags stuck in the sand before the stone gate, white coordinate numbers printed on the cloth） stands in the sand before the stone gate; Aida checks each number in turn.

Two brass bells（Two brass bells hanging under the tent eaves, bodies faintly glowing, chiming lightly when the wind rises） hang under the eaves of the excavation tent（A temporary excavation tent by the ruins, canvas flap open, surveying tools spread on the table）; Aida reaches out and lets them chime lightly.
Aida circles the stone gate, checking every crack.
Aida leans on a broken column, gazing at the darkening sand sea.

The intact cuneiform clay tablet（A brick-red clay tablet about two palms wide, face packed with cuneiform script, edges marked by ancient nicks） rests by the niche inside the stone gate, its cuneiform script clear.
Aida sits in the stone gate's shadow and rests in the afterglow.
Aida unrolls the forged parchment map（An aged pale-yellow parchment map ink-marked with oasis and ruins, a suspicious red-wax fake seal at the lower right）, matching it to the stone gate's bearing.
Aida pencils a suspicious route onto the forged parchment map.
Aida rolls up the forged parchment map and tucks it back into a canvas tube.
Sunset casts the cuneiform clay tablet's shadow onto the inner face of the stone gate.

At the edge of the sandstorm desert（Endless ochre dunes; when the wind rises, yellow sand blots out the sun and visibility collapses） at dawn, Aida greets young Nadia（Young Nadia: a lean desert apprentice girl of fourteen or fifteen, indigo headscarf, coarse sand-colored short robe, bright clear eyes） leading the pack camel（A sturdy sand-colored camel, saddlebags embroidered with blue geometric patterns, neck bell clear and bright）.
Nadia tethers the pack camel by a broken column and pats sand from the saddlebags.

Aida points to the three clay oil lamps（Three palm-sized clay oil lamps, dusted with sand, set in the niche inside the ruin stone gate） in the stone-gate niche and teaches Nadia to read their patterns.
Nadia crouches in the lee of a dune, curiously poking at dry scrub.
Aida explains dune direction and wind to Nadia.
Nadia looks back at the healthy pack camel, eyes full of longing.

In the palm-ringed oasis camp（A small oasis ringed by palms, a few beige tents, a shallow pool, camels tethered）, Hasan the guide（A steady desert guide in a sand-colored coarse cloak and deep-blue headscarf, wind-sand wrinkles on his left cheek, leading a camel） in a deep-blue headscarf looks back from behind a tent.
Hasan waters a camel at the shallow oasis pool.
Hasan tidies the ropes of a beige tent; the wrinkles on his left cheek deepen in the sunset.
Hasan leads a camel through the oasis camp.

On the sandstorm desert, Hasan and the masked bandit（A masked figure in the same sand-colored cloak, build close to Hasan's, ochre-red headscarf, curved blade at the waist, fierce eyes） face each other from afar—one in deep-blue headscarf, one in ochre-red.
Hasan shields the camel behind him; the bandit's curved blade slides half an inch from its sheath.
The bandit barks once and retreats into the sand dust; Hasan still stands his ground.
Hasan and the bandit each walk toward opposite dunes.
Months later at night, Aida alone tidies survey notes in the excavation tent.

Through her magnifying glass Aida spots the forged red-wax seal on the forged parchment map（The red-wax seal at the lower right of the parchment map has been exposed as forged; the surface is damp and wrinkled, ink lines bled）; the surface is already damp and wrinkled.
Aida wipes sand dust from the cuneiform clay tablet.
Aida lifts the tent flap and looks out at the black sand sea.
The cuneiform clay tablet lies quietly beside an oil lamp.
Through a long sand season, Aida clears the stone-gate reliefs day after day.
Another sandstorm night, Aida wraps her khaki coat tight and keeps watch inside the stone gate.
In spring drought, Aida stands before the stone gate watching distant mirages.
At high summer noon, Aida wipes a broken column scorched hot by the sun.
When autumn wind rises, the brick-red of the cuneiform clay tablet looks dull in the dust.
Another year-end, Aida alone keeps watch under the stone gate until dawn.
At daybreak Aida patrols the edge of the sandstorm desert, the healthy pack camel following behind.
Aida checks the stitching on the pack camel's saddlebags.
Aida steps into the stone gate; those three clay oil lamps still sit in the niche.

A sand-colored rental off-road vehicle（A brand-new sand-colored rental off-road vehicle with a spare tire strapped on the roof, nothing like a pack camel） drives past the dunes, spare tire on the roof—not a pack camel.
Aida stands on a dune recording wind shifts.
Aida hangs survey cord on a wooden rack in the lee of a dune.
A sandstorm rises suddenly; the ruin stone gate shudders in the gale.
Yellow sand pours into the stone gate; visibility collapses.
In her stumble Aida lets the cuneiform clay tablet（The cuneiform clay tablet has fallen onto rock; the brick-red face is burst into several shards） fall onto rock, and the brick-red face shatters.
On a distant dune the pack camel pitches hard in the storm.
A collapsing dune swallows the pack camel（The sand-colored camel lies dead in the lee of a dune, saddlebags scattered, neck bell silent）, and it dies where it falls.
Inside the stone gate Aida throws herself over the shattered cuneiform clay tablet shards and clutches them tight.
The day after the storm, Aida stands inside the stone gate staring at the shattered cuneiform clay tablet.
Aida runs a finger over the seam gaps of the cuneiform clay tablet, face dark.
Beside the excavation-tent log, Aida records the date the pack camel died.
An old photo of the pack camel hangs on the tent wall; Aida gazes at it a long time.
Aida pulls up one of the five survey flags in the sand and sits alone with the remnant.
Shards of the shattered cuneiform clay tablet still lie under the niche.
Weeks later, Aida spreads the shards in the excavation tent and begins reassembling the cuneiform clay tablet.

Aida takes a spare clay tablet（A blank spare clay tablet about half a palm large, color close to the cuneiform clay tablet but without script and with neater edges） from a wooden crate; it looks like the cuneiform clay tablet but has no script.
Aida carefully aligns the shards one by one.
The last seam closes, and the cuneiform clay tablet（The shards have been fitted piece by piece; the brick-red face shows complete cuneiform again, but seams remain visible） becomes reassembled.
The reassembled cuneiform clay tablet lies on the table; Aida looks at it with relief.

A sand-colored supply cart（A sand-colored supply trailer with canvas over the bed, shaped like a pack-animal supply unit but definitely not a camel） rolls to the dune edge, nothing like the pack camel now dead.
A bearded camp doctor（A lean camp doctor with a full beard, khaki vest, and canvas hat, build somewhat like Aida's） jumps down a dune and talks beside Aida; the two are similar in build.
The camp doctor points at the sand-colored supply cart and explains the new supply plan to Aida.
The sand-colored supply cart honks and drives off; Aida alone watches from the dune.

From the far side of the oasis comes a shepherd girl in a light-brown headscarf, Sana（A shepherd girl from the far side of the oasis, light-brown headscarf and dusty coarse robe; at a glance somewhat like young Nadia, but with shy unfamiliar eyes）—at a glance somewhat like young Nadia.
Sana tries drawing water at the shallow pool, but Aida shakes her head—she is not Nadia after all.

Years later at dusk, Aida（The same archaeologist wind-and-sand burned: canvas hat brim blackened, a fine crack in her goggles, cheeks sunburned and peeling, still wearing the magnifying glass） with sunburned cheeks stands under the palms of the oasis camp.
Aida looks up at the tent roof, gaze distant.
Those two brass bells under the tent eaves chime lightly in the wind; Aida pauses to listen.
Aida presses her palm to the tent's cold mast, as if saying goodbye.

In daylight, adult Nadia（Adult Nadia: a tall upright woman assistant in her twenties, still in indigo headscarf and sand-colored short robe, eyes firm） returns along the sand path, hurrying toward the oasis camp.
Nadia reunites with the burned Aida at camp; the two embrace.
Inside the tent, Nadia holds Aida's sand-dusted hands.

Aida（Aida has left the team to rest; only her canvas hat and magnifying glass remain at camp—she herself no longer appears） leaves her canvas hat and magnifying glass on the table, departs to rest away, and no longer appears.
Aida's canvas hat still lies on the tent table; Nadia reaches out and gently strokes it.

At the oasis edge, adult Nadia stands before a newly raised memorial stone slab（A sandstone slab standing at the oasis edge, carved with the archaeology captain's name and year, edges rounded by wind and sand）.
Nadia's fingertips trace Aida's name carved on the memorial stone slab.

Gray-haired Hasan the guide（Years later Hasan still wears the sand-colored cloak and deep-blue headscarf; temples gray, left-cheek wrinkles deeper） returns leading a new camel, sand-colored cloak and deep-blue headscarf as before.

The scarred masked bandit（The adult bandit still wears the ochre-red headscarf, masked with curved blade; a new scar shows under the face covering） flashes an ochre-red headscarf far on a dune, then vanishes.
Nadia and Hasan sit facing each other at a wooden table in the oasis camp.
The lens returns to years ago—the girl who learned the oil lamps before the stone-gate niche appears again.
That opening moment returns—inside the stone gate, an intact brick-red tablet is lifted out for the first time.
Flashback to the oasis of that year—a guide in a deep-blue headscarf, unmasked, flickers past.
Again the row of five small red flags appears before the stone gate.
Back to the half-buried stone-gate mouth of first meeting; sunset stretches shadows as of old.
Nadia unrolls again the debunked damp forged parchment map and walks into the excavation tent.
By the stone-gate niche, those three clay oil lamps still sit in place.
Nadia and Hasan guard the reassembled cuneiform clay tablet on the wooden table as sunset once more lights the stone gate.
